subject.title: Memory/QMD: isolate mcporter sidecars per agent

question: Should OpenClaw permanently own generated per-agent MCPorter configuration for bare QMD stdio servers while treating customized MCPorter definitions as externally owned?
rationale: Tests establish that the implementation works, but they cannot decide the long-term product boundary for generated configuration, user-owned credentials and lifecycle settings, daemon identity, and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Approve split ownership
options.body: Adopt the proposed boundary and require exact-head fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

options.title: Keep MCPorter external
options.body: Restrict OpenClaw to process-environment routing and avoid generating MCPorter configuration under agent state.

options.title: Pause for contract design
options.body: Hold the PR until supported MCPorter versions and configuration ownership are specified separately.

recommendation.title: Approve split ownership
recommendation.body: Adopt the proposed boundary and require exact-head fresh-install and upgrade proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent QMD manager and test history makes this person the strongest available routing candidate for the ownership decision.
